newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Coats restructure on course.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Coats restructure on course.

text.p: Textiles group Coats Viyella Plc said on Wednesday that its 55 million stg restructuring programme is on course, and the remaining 38 million pounds of costs will all be charged against second half earnings.

Chief executive Neville Bain said in a telephone interview with Reuters that although some cash payments may be held over to 1997 "charges will be taken this year so 1997 will be put on a clean basis going forward."
Reorganisation costs of 17.2 million pounds were charged against first half earnings, helping push pretax profit down 34 percent to 47.0 million stg from 70.8 million.
Bain said he is confident the group will achieve its cumulative annual cost saving targets of 10 million pounds in the second half of 1996, 25 million pounds in 1997 and 35 million in 1998.

However, he said not all of this will reach the bottom line as the group invests in moving much of its clothing production to lower-cost countries. The reorganisation involves shedding 7,750 jobs, including nearly 3,000 in the UK.
Bain said Coats is attracted by Morocco, eastern Europe and "parts of Asia." The company already operates in Poland and Hungary and is mow examining opportunites in Romania.

First half operating profits on continuing operations slipped to 78.0 million stg from 87.3 million. Bain said much of the fall was down to the thread division, "largely due to Brazil and Turkey in the first-half of 1995 having exceptional levels of profits. We said at the time that was unsustainable."
Coats said it expects an improvement in second -half results year-on-year before charges, with the key September to Decemeber period accounting for half its annual profits.
"We think we know what the number is going to be but it wouldn't be appropriate to make forecasts," Bain said, adding that "all the evidence is that (the rise) will be worthwhile."

After a "difficult" first half, Coats said trading conditions "appear to be showing some signs of improvement," with a return of U.K. consumer confidence and normal weather patterns expected to help second-half performance.

Bain said there is "continued progress" at the Jaeger and Viyella fashion retail chains, and the group's home furnishings business is benefiting from a pick up in the U.K. housing market "which is substantial and we think it will be sustained."
"The USA is picking up and we think it will good to us, especially in threads and engineering," Bain added.
Demand in the rest of Europe is expected to remain mixed.
Coats said the outlook for Brazil is "somewhat uncertain," although it added that current profitability there is "at satisfactory levels."
Bain declined to be drawn on when Coats will return to increasing its dividend, repeating the company's goal of building dividend cover to two times.
After reorganisation charges in the first half of the year, the dividend was barely covered by earnings per share.
